harmonicFunction: F#5 (i in F# minor) - Dark tonic pedal for the intro riff, establishes the heavy metal foundation
A (I in A major) - Bright tonic of the relative major, anchors verse and chorus sections
E (V) - Dominant chord providing strong resolution tension in both keys
D (IV) - Subdominant adding warmth and forward motion
F#m (vi) - Natural minor chord connecting the two key centers of the song
Tritone interval (F# to C) - The devil's interval creating the riff's signature tension and menace

techniques.name: Tritone-Based Intro Riff
techniques.description: Randy Rhoads's iconic intro riff built on an F#5 power chord with a tritone interval (augmented 4th/diminished 5th), combining rapid alternate picking with the most dissonant interval in music for a driving, unsettling effect

notes: The riff centers on F# (2nd fret low E string) as the root
The tritone interval uses C natural (8th fret low E string) against F#
Rapid alternate picking on the low E string at 138 BPM
The riff uses a galloping rhythmic pattern: eighth-note, two sixteenth-notes
Pattern: F#-F#-A-F#-F#-B-A-F#-E-F# on the low E string
Must maintain tight palm muting except on accent notes
sequence: Begin with palm-muted alternate picking on F# (2nd fret, low E string)
Execute the tritone leap to C natural and back
Maintain the galloping rhythm pattern throughout
Use downstroke accents on the strong beats
Keep palm muting tight for the percussive, chugging sound
The riff repeats with slight variations before the verse
tips: Start at half speed (70 BPM) and gradually build to 138 BPM
Focus on clean alternate picking before adding speed
The palm muting pressure controls the tone - too heavy kills sustain, too light loses punch
Use a metronome religiously - the riff must be metronomically precise
Practice the tritone interval leap in isolation before integrating
details.progression: F#5-based single-note riff with tritone interval

techniques.name: Fast Alternate Picking
techniques.description: Rapid alternate picking technique essential for the intro riff and verse rhythm, requiring precise down-up-down-up motion at 138 BPM with palm muting control

notes: Strict alternating downstroke/upstroke pattern at high tempo
Pick angle should be slightly angled for speed and efficiency
Wrist-based motion, not arm - keep the forearm stationary
Pick grip should be firm but not tense
Combine with palm muting for rhythm sections
Release palm mute on accent notes for dynamic contrast
sequence: Begin with open string alternate picking at 80 BPM
Add palm muting while maintaining clean alternate strokes
Introduce the F# pedal tone riff pattern at slow tempo
Gradually increase tempo in 10 BPM increments
Build to full 138 BPM while maintaining clarity
tips: Economy of motion is critical - minimize pick travel distance
Keep your wrist relaxed; tension is the enemy of speed
Practice with a clean tone first to hear picking inconsistencies
Set a metronome and only increase tempo when the current speed is effortless
Take breaks to prevent repetitive strain - speed builds over weeks, not hours
details.progression: Single-note alternate picking across all riff sections

techniques.name: Classical-Influenced Solo Phrasing
techniques.description: Randy Rhoads's revolutionary approach of blending classical music techniques with rock guitar, featuring sequenced scale runs, arpeggiated patterns, and precise legato phrases that defined a new era of guitar playing

notes: Based primarily in F# minor pentatonic with added classical scale passages
Uses sequenced patterns (groups of 4 or 6 notes) ascending and descending
Incorporates sweep-picked arpeggios across multiple strings
Vibrato technique: wide, controlled classical-style vibrato
String bending with precise pitch targeting (whole and half steps)
Legato runs using hammer-ons and pull-offs for fluid passages
sequence: Learn the F# minor pentatonic positions used in the solo
Practice the sequenced scale runs in groups of four notes
Work on the arpeggio patterns across strings 1-4
Develop the wide vibrato on sustained notes
Connect individual phrases into the complete solo
Practice with backing track for context and timing
tips: Break the solo into 4-bar phrases and learn each individually
Randy's vibrato comes from the wrist, not the fingers - practice this specifically
The classical sequences follow specific intervallic patterns - analyze the theory
Use a slow-downer app to practice at 50%, 75%, then full speed
This solo is a masterclass in composition - every note has purpose
details.progression: Over F#m - D - A - E solo backing progression

sections.name: Intro Riff
sections.description: One of the most recognizable guitar riffs in heavy metal history - the driving F#-based riff with its signature tritone interval that launches the song with pure adrenaline
sections.progression: F#5 pedal tone riff with tritone (C natural) interval
notes: Palm-muted alternate picking at 138 BPM on the low E string
The tritone interval (F# to C) creates the riff's signature menacing sound
Galloping rhythm pattern gives the riff its driving momentum
Start slowly and build speed - accuracy trumps velocity

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: The song shifts to A major for the verse, with palm-muted power chord rhythm supporting Ozzy's vocal melody with a more open, melodic feel
notes: Shift from F# minor riff to A major power chords
Palm-muted chugging between chord accents
Power chords should ring on accent beats, muted between
Maintain the driving energy while allowing the vocal to lead

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The explosive the signature chorus with full power chord strumming and maximum energy
notes: Full, open power chords with less palm muting than verse
Maximum strumming intensity for the anthemic chorus
Quick D to A transition at the end needs to be clean
The energy peak of each verse-chorus cycle

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: Randy Rhoads's legendary guitar solo combining classical technique with rock intensity - featuring sequenced runs, sweep arpeggios, precise bending, and his signature wide vibrato over a cycling chord progression
notes: Solo positions span from 12th to 17th fret primarily
Sequenced scale runs in groups of four notes are the foundation
Wide, controlled vibrato on sustained notes is Randy's signature
Each phrase has a clear beginning, development, and resolution
Break into 4-bar segments for learning - do not try to learn all at once

guitar.recommended: Gibson Les Paul Custom (Randy Rhoads model)
alternatives: Any humbucker-equipped solid body with good upper fret access
guitar.pickup: High-output humbuckers for thick distortion tone and sustain

settings.presence: 7-8 (bite and cut for the riff attack)

effects.distortion: MXR Distortion+ (Randy's primary overdrive pedal, pushing the Marshall into heavy saturation)
effects.delay: Short delay (100-200ms) for lead solo sections
effects.reverb: Light spring reverb from the amp
effects.other: MXR 10-Band EQ for tone shaping. Wah pedal (Cry Baby) for occasional solo accents.

beginner.focus: Learn the simplified verse power chords and basic rhythm pattern
steps: Master A5, E5, D5, and F#5 power chord shapes
Practice basic alternate picking on single strings at slow tempo
Learn the verse chord progression: A - E - F#m - D with simple strumming
Work on palm muting technique with power chords

intermediate.focus: Learn the intro riff at reduced tempo and verse/chorus with proper technique
steps: Practice the intro riff pattern slowly at 70-80 BPM
Build alternate picking speed incrementally toward 138 BPM
Master the palm muting dynamics for verse and chorus contrast
Learn the tritone interval and its placement in the riff
Play through the complete song structure with transitions

advanced.focus: Master the intro riff at full speed and tackle the guitar solo
steps: Achieve clean intro riff execution at full 138 BPM
Break the guitar solo into individual phrases and learn each
Develop wide vibrato technique for sustained solo notes
Practice sequenced scale runs and arpeggio patterns
Perform the complete song with both rhythm and lead parts
advanced.timeEstimate: 3-6 months for complete mastery including solo

commonMistakes: Trying to play the intro riff at full speed before mastering it slowly
Inconsistent palm muting - too heavy kills the tone, too light loses definition
Sloppy alternate picking with uneven downstroke/upstroke volume
Neglecting the tritone interval accuracy in the intro riff
Tensing up the picking hand when increasing speed
practiceRoutine: Warm up with alternate picking exercises on open strings for 5 minutes
Practice the intro riff at 70% speed with a metronome for 10 minutes
Work on power chord transitions: A-E-F#m-D at full tempo (5 minutes)
Palm muting dynamics drill: alternate between muted and open power chords (5 minutes)
Solo phrase work: isolate one 4-bar solo phrase per session (10 minutes)
Full song play-through at current comfortable tempo
focusAreas: Tritone interval accuracy in the intro riff
metronomeWork: Start the intro riff at 70 BPM and increase by 5 BPM per session
Practice verse power chords at 100 BPM, building to 138 BPM
Alternate picking single-string exercises: 80 BPM to 160 BPM progressively
Solo phrases at 50% speed with metronome, gradually approaching full tempo
